flyer.description: Print a flyer with a QR code and FIND Food Bank's phone number to help people find free food.
flyerLead: Print this page and post it where people wait: the laundromat, the clinic, the church, the school office. Anyone can scan the code or call the number.
flyerStep1: Print on letter paper. Black and white is fine, and it photocopies well.
flyerStep2: Cut the strips at the bottom along the lines so people can take the number with them.
flyerStep3: Ask before you put it up on a board.
flyerNoJs: To print, use your browser's menu (Ctrl+P or ⌘P).
sheetScan: Scan with your phone camera to see food pantries, mobile markets and hot meals, and which places are open today.

about.ogTitle: About this site · Acerca de este sitio
about.ogDescription: Who made comidacoachellavalley, where its information comes from, how accessible it is, and how to report a problem or suggest a place.
about.ogImageAlt: comidacoachellavalley: Free food in the Coachella Valley. Comida gratis en el Valle de Coachella.
aboutLead: A free food finder for the Coachella Valley, in Spanish and English.
aboutWhat1: comidacoachellavalley lists food pantries, mobile markets and places that serve hot meals across the Coachella Valley. Search by name, city or street, see what is open today, then call or get directions.
aboutWhat2: It was made by students for the California State Seal of Civic Engagement. It is not run by FIND Food Bank. The aim is simple: finding food near you should take a few taps. Spanish comes first, and the Spanish text for each place is our own translation of the English.
aboutSource1: Most places come from FIND Food Bank's public map and its monthly Mobile Market calendar. Where the two disagree, we use the calendar.
aboutSource2: A few places run by churches and community groups come from the organization's own website. Each one shows where its information came from and the date we checked it, and it shows a warning if it has not been checked in 90 days.
aboutSource3: A script compares our list with FIND's page every week, and anything that differs is flagged for a person to look at. Hours change, so please call before you go. The map spots used by the "sort by distance" button come from OpenStreetMap contributors.
aboutAccess1: We want everyone to be able to use this site. What we have built in:
aboutAccessA: Large text and buttons that are easy to tap.
aboutAccessB: The whole site works with a keyboard, with a clear outline showing where you are, and a "skip to the list" link at the top.
aboutAccessC: Text colors that we checked for contrast, in a light and a dark version that follows your device.
aboutAccessD: Animation that stops if your device is set to reduce motion.
aboutAccessE: The list of places also shows with JavaScript turned off.
aboutAccess2: What we have not done yet: we have not had the site tested by people who use screen readers or other assistive tools, so there may be problems we have not found. If something does not work for you, please tell us.
aboutHelp1: Wrong hours, a place that has closed, a wrong phone number? Every place has a "Report a problem" link.
aboutHelp2: Know a place that is missing? A place is listed only if the organization's own website or an official source says it gives out free food, with a street address, days and times, and the information is less than a year old.
aboutHelp3: These links need a free GitHub account. If you need food now or cannot use GitHub, call FIND Food Bank:
